assessment.governing_intent: Produce operational evidence that the canonical monitor_host liveness composition, not the SWF-29 bootstrap, delivers four behaviours under real transport and wall-clock time: lost-trigger recovery within G+I, provider/judgment suppression with attributed resolution, restart and delayed-delivery duplicate safety with one writer, and exact outcome readback. Phase 1 proves the mechanics on an isolated synthetic profile. Phase 2 closes SF-REQ-056-AC-08 against the real factory workload. Neither phase retires the bootstrap.
implementation_unknowns: Whether monitor_host/LivenessProfile already has an adapter that observes the real dispatcher `active` map and Project #1 lane state and performs board mutations, or whether one must be built. The text reports phase 1 as sqlite-store-only.
Exact fx-b2-supervision.json contents and the systemd-run unit naming for the isolated profile.
How to apply the FX-B7-shaped evidence schema to a two-phase record that keeps phase-1 and phase-2 labels distinct.
How to run the pre-flight check that no other active-map entry is within its grace window, and how to read the whole board to confirm no other lane was affected.
How to time SIGTERM and restart in step 5 so it lands after a durable intent exists but before readback settles, on real wall-clock time.
material_risks: Custody of the `systemctl --user stop/start alienintent-liveness.service` pair is assigned to 'the actor executing IMPLEMENT/VERIFY'. The window spans the PRODUCER-to-VERIFIER handoff, so it is unclear which actor must guarantee the restart. An unrecovered stop leaves the real factory without bootstrap supervision.
If both the bootstrap and monitor_host are active, or the pause is misordered, the same Project #1 status could be mutated twice.
The 2026-09-28 section appears to overstate an earlier Founder disposition. Relying on it could produce a DONE claim the Founder did not authorize.
A NO_GAP_OBSERVED outcome plus synthetic probes could be presented as AC-08 closure, contrary to the explicit rule that offline, sandbox or synthetic success alone fails.
Authority for phase 2 is reported via relayed inbox handoffs from an observing session. This gate cannot independently verify those records.
Phase 2 may require new real-board and state.json adapters, which the node's scope and architecture constraints may not cover.
assessment.next_action: Route the three phase-2 questions to the Founder via the Program Director: whether NO_GAP_OBSERVED or a synthetic continuation is acceptable, whether the self-referential #125 target counts as 'that workload', and whether real board mutation by monitor_host is in scope. Also have the Director pin a single named custodian for the bootstrap stop/start across the handoff. Record the answers durably and resubmit this revision for assessment. Phase 1 may proceed as bounded engineering proof under the existing allocation meanwhile, as the record already permits, without any DONE or AC-08 claim.
owner_clarifications: AC-08 requires demonstrating lost-trigger recovery 'on that workload'. If the #125 lane completes inside grace, does a phase-2 run that records NO_GAP_OBSERVED satisfy AC-08 when recovery, suppression and duplicate probes run only against a 'deliberately held-open synthetic continuation' of that lane? If not, is the producer authorized to deliberately induce a genuine gap on #125's own real lane (for example by withholding or delaying VERIFIER dispatch), and within what bounds?

Does the Founder, not the Director's reading of the 2026-09-27 record, accept this BIU's own #125 PRODUCER/VERIFIER dispatch lane as AC-08's 'that workload'? This matters because the subject of the proof is the same execution whose producer runs the fixture and whose verifier must independently judge it. The 2026-09-27 disposition predates this binding and does not itself say this target counts.

Phase 2 has monitor_host issue real `gh project item-edit` mutations on Project #1 and read the real dispatcher state.json. Is that within the pinned design and node extent as an existing capability, or does it need a reviewed design/SPECIFY disposition? The architecture constraints forbid context boundaries beyond the pinned design, and the Founder's R1-GAP-MONITOR-HOST disposition was scoped narrowly to the monitor_host composition.
assessment.rationale: The controlling condition is unresolved owner intent about what evidence satisfies the BIU's own completion predicate. It is not missing prerequisites, since the target, budget and custody are reported as bound. It is not independent decision centers either, since the Founder deliberately kept both phases in one BIU and phase 2 depends on phase 1. The phase-2 plan defines a likely success path (no gap, probes against a synthetic continuation) that appears to contradict the Founder's recorded rule that synthetic subjects do not satisfy AC-08. It also chooses a self-referential subject that weakens independent verification, and it cites a prior disposition as settling a question that disposition predates. These are acceptance and authority questions only the Founder can answer. Engineering research cannot resolve them, and handing off now would likely cause rework or an unsupported DONE claim.
assessment.summary: Phase 1 appears handoff-ready as the text reports it. The target, isolated profile, policy, seven pinned fixture steps, evidence schema, budget and custody are all stated, and the Founder has disposed the owner questions for it. Phase 2 is not ready. It is also part of this BIU's completion predicate (DONE), and the Founder kept both phases in one BIU. Three problems block it. First, the target chosen is this BIU's own #125 PRODUCER-to-VERIFIER lane, observed while that same execution is running. Second, the text calls the normal outcome (NO_GAP_OBSERVED, with probes run against a 'deliberately held-open synthetic continuation') valid. That appears to conflict with the Founder's 2026-09-27 disposition that synthetic subjects do not satisfy AC-08's 'that workload'. Third, the 2026-09-28 section says the 'that workload' question was already answered with 'this bound target counts'. But the 2026-09-27 disposition predates the binding and left the phase-2 target unbound, so the record contradicts itself on a material acceptance question.
assessment.verification_assessment: Phase 1 acceptance is observable. The seven steps have pinned commands, expected refusal codes, durable sqlite readbacks and an evidence schema, so a fresh verifier on the exact SHA can give a meaningful verdict on mechanics. Phase 2 acceptance is not reliably observable as written. Its central predicate, lost-trigger recovery on the real workload, depends on a gap that may not occur, and the fallback path uses a synthetic continuation. The subject of the proof is the producer-to-verifier handoff of the same BIU, which weakens the verifier's independence. So a single independent verdict on BIU completion (AC-08/DONE) is not meaningful until the owner fixes what phase-2 evidence counts.
